details:
To reproduce this issue, open any new or pre-existing Avatar project via the CC.

Start by creating a new Surface shader by right clicking in the Assets window, and going to Create > Shader > Standard Surface Shader. Do *not* edit this shader's code. *Do* apply any texture so that it can be rendered in a recognizable way.

Once this is done, apply this shader to the avatar and upload the avatar. Use the avatar. Upon using the avatar, the local avatar appears diffuse white, and on remote players, they see the magenta error color.

This issue also occurs with unlit shaders (shaders that do not use Unity's built in surface system, and instead manually declare a vertex and fragment program).

This is affecting all uploads as of this post. This has also been tested and confirmed by a friend of mine. I'll do more testing to try to find more patterns. Changing worlds and restarting the client did not help.

**Important notes:**

- The shader I first noticed this issue on explicitly disabled instanced rendering. I also tried implementing instancing into my shader, and this had no effect.

- The avatar *does* properly render in the menu's avatar preview.

- Hiding and reshowing someone will inconsistently display the avatar properly for what appears to be a single frame.

**Edit:**

This issue has is more inconsistent than I initially saw, I will need to continue testing but if I can't get it to happen consistently I may need to remove this post.
title: Custom shaders no longer render in the world for new uploads
